resolved_by: Supreme Court in United States v. Davis, 139 S. Ct. 2319 (2019), which abrogated Ovalles and held the § 924(c)(3)(B) residual clause unconstitutionally vague
issue: Is the residual clause of 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(3)(B) void for vagueness, or can courts avoid that problem by applying a conduct-based rather than categorical approach?

sides.position: The § 924(c)(3)(B) residual clause operates in the present and can be applied through a conduct-based approach, so it avoids the vagueness problem that affected the ACCA and § 16(b) residual clauses
cases: United States v. Ovalles, 905 F.3d 1231 (11th Cir. 2018) (en banc), abrogated by United States v. Davis, 139 S. Ct. 2319 (2019)
Jones v. United States, No. 20-13365 (11th Cir. 2023)

quote: As it turned out, the Supreme Court rejected that distinction, abrogating our Ovalles decision and settling a circuit split.
cite: Charles Edward Jones v. United States, No. 20-13365 (11th Cir. 2023)
